course.title: Nigerian Cooking
course.tagline: Cook jollof, soups, stews and local favourites the way they are meant to taste.

days.title: The Nigerian Kitchen: Tools and Staples
days.goal: Set up your kitchen with the staples of Nigerian cooking.

video.title: How To Cook Perfect Party Jollof Rice: Tips for Smoky Nigerian Party Jollof Rice

steps: Stock the basics: rice, garri, yam, palm oil, groundnut oil, crayfish, stock cubes, peppers.
Learn the pepper mix: tatashe (bell pepper), scotch bonnet and onion blended together.
Keep a clean mortar or blender ready for grinding egusi, ogbono and crayfish.
Taste palm oil, crayfish and iru (locust beans) so you know their flavours.
Cook plain white rice and keep it for tomorrow's stew.
days.task: Buy or list your Nigerian pantry staples and blend one pepper mix.
days.challenge: Blend a pepper mix without water so it fries faster and tastes richer.

quiz.q: What three things go into a basic Nigerian pepper mix?
quiz.explain: Tatashe, scotch bonnet and onion blended together is the base of most Nigerian stews.

quiz.q: Why blend pepper mix without water?
options: It fries faster and tastes richer
quiz.explain: A dry blend fries down quickly and gives a deeper, less sour stew.

quiz.q: What is iru?
options: Fermented locust beans used for flavour
quiz.explain: Iru (locust beans) adds a deep, savoury flavour to soups and stews.

days.title: Perfect White Rice and Stew Basics
days.goal: Cook fluffy white rice and a simple tomato stew.

video.title: Perfect Jollof Rice - Goat Meat Jollof Rice | Tips for Smoky Party Jollof

steps: Rinse rice until the water runs clear, then boil in salted water.
Blend tatashe, scotch bonnet and onion with a little tomato.
Fry the blend in groundnut oil until it darkens and the oil floats on top.
Season with stock cubes, salt and crayfish; add boiled meat or fish.
Serve the stew over the rice with a boiled egg if you like.
days.task: Cook white rice and tomato stew from scratch.
days.challenge: Fry the stew until the oil separates on top, then compare the taste with a quickly fried stew.

quiz.q: How do you know tomato stew is well fried?
options: The oil separates and floats on top
quiz.explain: When the oil floats on top and the stew darkens, the raw tomato taste is gone.

quiz.q: Why rinse rice before cooking?
options: To remove starch so it stays separate
quiz.explain: Rinsing removes surface starch so the grains stay fluffy and separate.

quiz.q: What does crayfish add to stew?
quiz.explain: Ground crayfish gives Nigerian stews their characteristic savoury depth.

days.title: Party Jollof Rice: The Smoky Secret
days.goal: Cook smoky party jollof rice the way it is done at Nigerian parties.

video.title: Oven Baked Jollof Rice

steps: Blend peppers and fry the base in oil until dark and rich.
Add tomato paste and fry it well so it loses its sour taste.
Add stock, season, and stir in washed rice.
Cover tightly with foil and a lid, cook on low heat without stirring.
Let the bottom catch slightly for the smoky party flavour, then fluff.
days.task: Cook a pot of party jollof rice.
days.challenge: Cook it again using the foil-and-lid method and see if the smoke flavour appears.

quiz.q: What gives party jollof its smoky flavour?
options: The rice catching slightly at the bottom of the pot
quiz.explain: A slight catch at the bottom of the pot gives the famous smoky taste.

quiz.q: Why cover the pot with foil and a lid?
options: To trap steam so the rice cooks evenly
quiz.explain: A tight seal traps steam so the rice cooks evenly without burning.

quiz.q: Why fry tomato paste before adding rice?
options: To remove its raw, sour taste
quiz.explain: Unfried tomato paste tastes sour and raw; frying it deepens the flavour.

days.title: Jollof Rice Variations
days.goal: Cook jollof with goat meat, chicken or vegetables.

video.title: Perfect Jollof Rice with Peppered Beef

steps: Boil your protein with onion, seasoning and a little water to make stock.
Use the stock as the cooking liquid for the jollof.
Add the cooked meat on top to steam with the rice, or fry it separately.
Try a vegetable jollof with carrots, peas and sweetcorn.
Serve with fried plantain and a simple salad.
days.task: Cook jollof rice with a protein of your choice using homemade stock.
days.challenge: Cook a vegetable jollof and compare the cooking time with the meat version.

quiz.q: Why cook jollof in meat stock instead of water?
options: Stock adds flavour the rice absorbs
quiz.explain: Rice cooked in stock absorbs all that flavour.

quiz.q: What should you add to jollof last?
options: Delicate vegetables like peas, so they stay bright
quiz.explain: Peas and sweetcorn added late stay bright and do not go mushy.

quiz.q: What is the best partner for jollof at a party?
quiz.explain: Fried plantain is the classic partner for jollof rice.

days.title: Egusi Soup from Scratch
days.goal: Cook egusi soup with the frying method.

video.title: Ogbono Egusi Combo Recipe

steps: Grind egusi seeds into a fine powder.
Mix the egusi with a little water into a thick paste.
Fry onion and pepper in palm oil, then add the egusi in lumps and fry until it firms up.
Add stock, meat and fish, then simmer.
Add ugu or bitter leaf at the end and cook for 5 minutes.
days.task: Cook egusi soup using the frying method.
days.challenge: Try the boiling method another day and decide which texture you prefer.

quiz.q: What is egusi made from?
quiz.explain: Egusi is ground melon seed, the thickener and heart of the soup.

quiz.q: Why fry egusi in lumps?
options: So it forms firm, crumbly lumps instead of a smooth paste
quiz.explain: Frying egusi in lumps gives the classic crumbly texture.

quiz.q: When do leafy vegetables go into egusi soup?
options: Near the end, so they stay green and fresh
quiz.explain: Leaves added late stay green and keep their nutrients.

days.title: Ogbono Soup: The Draw Soup
days.goal: Cook ogbono soup, with or without egusi.

video.title: How to Make Ogbono Soup (Frying Method)

steps: Grind ogbono seeds into a smooth powder.
Heat palm oil, add the ogbono and stir until it melts and draws.
Add stock gradually, stirring so it does not go lumpy.
Add meat, fish, crayfish and seasoning, then simmer.
Add ugu leaves and cook for 5 minutes. Serve with a swallow.
days.task: Cook ogbono soup and eat it with garri or fufu.
days.challenge: Cook an ogbono and egusi combo and note how the texture changes.

quiz.q: What makes ogbono soup draw?
options: The natural thickener in ground ogbono seeds
quiz.explain: Ogbono seeds contain a natural thickener that gives the soup its draw.

quiz.q: Why add stock gradually to ogbono?
quiz.explain: Adding liquid slowly while stirring keeps the soup smooth.

quiz.q: What is a 'swallow'?
options: A starchy dough like eba or fufu eaten with soup
quiz.explain: Swallows are starchy doughs, eba, fufu or pounded yam, used to scoop soup.

days.title: Week 1 Project: Jollof and Egusi Feast
days.goal: Cook jollof rice and egusi soup for your household in one session.

video.title: How to Make Ogbono Soup (Boiling Method)

steps: Plan the menu: party jollof, egusi soup, a swallow, and fried plantain.
Write a shopping list and buy everything in one trip.
Start the soup first since it simmers longest.
Cook the jollof while the soup simmers.
Serve everything together and get feedback.
days.task: Cook jollof rice and egusi soup in one session.
days.challenge: Serve the meal to a guest and ask which dish they liked best.

quiz.q: Why start the soup before the jollof?
options: Soup simmers longest, so it starts first
quiz.explain: Start with what takes longest so everything finishes together.

quiz.q: What is the key to smoky party jollof?
options: A slight catch at the bottom of the pot
quiz.explain: The slight catch at the bottom gives the smoky party flavour.

quiz.q: What should a Nigerian feast have?
options: A rice dish, a soup, a swallow and a side
quiz.explain: A proper spread balances rice, soup, swallow and a side like plantain.

project.title: Cook a Jollof and Egusi Feast
project.brief: Cook party jollof rice and egusi soup with a swallow and plantain in one session.
checks: Menu planned with a shopping list
Pepper base fried until oil separates
Jollof cooked with a smoky finish, not burnt
Egusi soup with correct crumbly texture
Swallow and plantain served with the meal
Feedback collected from the people who ate

days.title: Afang Soup and Edikang Ikong
days.goal: Cook Afang soup and its cousin Edikang Ikong.

video.title: How to Cook Egusi and Ogbono Soup

steps: Wash and slice waterleaf and Afang (okazi) leaves finely.
Boil meat and stockfish with seasoning to make a rich stock.
Add palm oil, crayfish and pepper to the stock.
Add waterleaf first, let it release water, then add Afang.
Simmer 10 minutes and serve with fufu or garri.
days.task: Cook Afang soup.
days.challenge: Cook Edikang Ikong another day and compare the leaf combinations.

quiz.q: What two leaves make Afang soup?
quiz.explain: Afang uses waterleaf and Afang leaves.

quiz.q: Why add waterleaf before Afang?
options: Waterleaf releases water that cooks the soup
quiz.explain: Waterleaf gives out water as it cooks, forming the soup base.

quiz.q: Where does Afang soup come from?
options: The Efik and Ibibio people of the South-South
quiz.explain: Afang is a classic soup of the Efik and Ibibio people.

days.title: Ayamase (Ofada Stew) and Ofada Rice
days.goal: Cook the green pepper stew that goes with Ofada rice.

video.title: How to Cook Ogbono Soup with Egusi

steps: Blend green peppers, green scotch bonnet and onion.
Boil the blend to remove water, then fry in palm oil.
Add iru, crayfish and assorted meats.
Cook Ofada rice separately until soft and slightly sticky.
Serve the stew over the rice with boiled eggs.
days.task: Cook Ayamase and Ofada rice.
days.challenge: Try Ayamase with white rice and note the difference.

quiz.q: What gives Ayamase its green colour?
options: Green peppers and green scotch bonnet
quiz.explain: Ayamase is made from green peppers, which give it its colour and flavour.

quiz.q: What is iru and why is it in Ayamase?
options: Fermented locust beans that give a deep savoury flavour
quiz.explain: Iru is essential to Ayamase's flavour.

quiz.q: What rice goes with Ayamase?
options: Ofada rice, a local short-grain rice
quiz.explain: Ofada rice is the traditional partner, with its nutty flavour.

days.title: Nigerian Stew: The Everyday Pot
days.goal: Cook a big pot of Nigerian tomato stew to last the week.

video.title: Fresh Plantain Fufu

steps: Blend a large pepper mix and boil off the water.
Fry in oil until dark and the oil separates.
Add stock, seasoning, crayfish and your proteins.
Simmer 20 minutes, then taste and adjust salt and heat.
Cool, portion and freeze in containers for the week.
days.task: Cook a large pot of stew and portion it for the week.
days.challenge: Use the stew three ways: with rice, with yam, and with bread.

quiz.q: Why boil the pepper mix before frying?
options: To remove water so it fries faster and tastes less sour
quiz.explain: Boiling off the water first shortens frying time and improves flavour.

quiz.q: How long does stew keep in the fridge?
quiz.explain: Cooked stew keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge; freeze it for longer.

quiz.q: What is the sign of a well-fried stew?
options: Oil floats on top and it smells rich, not raw
quiz.explain: Oil separation and a rich smell mean the raw tomato taste is gone.

days.title: Yam Porridge and Yam Dishes
days.goal: Cook yam porridge and fried yam with stew.

video.title: Nigerian Afang Soup Recipe

steps: Peel yam, cut into chunks and rinse.
Boil yam in pepper mix, palm oil and stock until soft.
Mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken the porridge.
Add scent leaf or ugu at the end.
For fried yam, cut into fingers, salt, and fry until golden.
days.task: Cook yam porridge.
days.challenge: Cook fried yam with stew the next day and compare.

quiz.q: How do you thicken yam porridge?
options: Mash some yam pieces into the pot
quiz.explain: Mashing a few soft yam pieces thickens the porridge naturally.

quiz.q: What leaf is often added to yam porridge?
quiz.explain: Scent leaf adds a fresh aroma to yam porridge.

quiz.q: Why rinse cut yam?
options: To remove surface starch and dirt
quiz.explain: Rinsing removes starch and any dirt from peeling.

days.title: Suya: Marinade and Grilling
days.goal: Make suya spice and grill suya at home.

video.title: How to Make Ayamase (Ofada Stew/Sauce)

steps: Mix the suya spice: ground peanuts, ginger, paprika, chilli and salt.
Cut beef thinly and marinate with oil and the spice mix.
Thread onto skewers and grill over charcoal or in the oven.
Turn often and brush with oil so it stays moist.
Serve with sliced onion, cabbage and extra suya spice.
days.task: Make suya at home with homemade suya spice.
days.challenge: Grill suya chicken the same way and compare.

quiz.q: What is the base of suya spice (yaji)?
quiz.explain: Yaji is built on ground peanuts with ginger, paprika and chilli.

quiz.q: Why cut suya meat thinly?
options: Thin slices cook fast and take on more spice
It is easier to chew only
quiz.explain: Thin slices grill quickly and carry more spice on their surface.

quiz.q: What is suya traditionally served with?
options: Sliced onion and cabbage with extra spice
quiz.explain: Onion and cabbage with extra yaji are the classic suya accompaniments.

days.title: Peppered Beef, Chicken and Fish
days.goal: Make peppered proteins for parties and small chops.

video.title: How to Cook Nigerian Stew

steps: Boil or grill your protein first until cooked.
Fry a thick pepper mix with onion until the oil separates.
Add the protein and toss so every piece is coated.
Cook on low for 5 minutes so the pepper clings.
Serve as a side or as small chops at a party.
days.task: Cook peppered chicken.
days.challenge: Cook peppered fish and note how the cooking time differs.

quiz.q: Why cook the protein before adding the pepper mix?
options: So the pepper coats cooked meat instead of stewing raw meat
quiz.explain: Pre-cooked protein absorbs the pepper sauce without overcooking.

quiz.q: What makes a pepper mix thick enough to coat meat?
options: Frying it down until most water evaporates
quiz.explain: A well-fried, reduced pepper mix clings to meat instead of sliding off.

quiz.q: What is peppered meat often served as?
quiz.explain: Peppered chicken, beef and fish are classic party small chops.

days.title: Week 2 Project: Cook a Party Spread
days.goal: Cook a small party spread: rice, soup, suya and peppered chicken.

video.title: How to Cook Beef Stir Fry Vegetable

steps: Choose the menu and write a shopping list with costs.
Start the soup and stew first; grill suya last so it is hot.
Cook the rice while the soup simmers.
Plate everything on a big tray, party style.
Serve to family or friends and ask for honest feedback.
days.task: Cook a party spread for at least 4 people.
days.challenge: Cost the whole spread and work out the price per person.

quiz.q: What should you cook last at a party?
options: Grilled items like suya, so they are hot
quiz.explain: Grilled food goes cold fast, so it is cooked last.

quiz.q: Why cost a party spread per person?
options: So you can price it if you ever sell it
quiz.explain: Knowing the cost per person is the first step to selling food.

quiz.q: What makes a good party spread?
options: A mix of rice, soup, grilled and peppered dishes
quiz.explain: Variety is what makes a party table feel like a party.

project.title: Cook a Party Spread
project.brief: Cook a spread of rice, soup, suya and peppered chicken for at least 4 people.
checks: Menu planned with costs per person
Soup and stew cooked and well seasoned
Rice cooked fluffy with a smoky finish
Suya grilled and served hot
Peppered chicken coated and tasty
Spread served together and feedback collected

days.title: Swallows: Eba, Fufu and Pounded Yam
days.goal: Make smooth, lump-free swallows.

video.title: How to Cook Beef Stir Fried Rice

steps: Eba: boil water, pour in garri gradually while stirring hard, then knead.
Fufu: mix cassava flour with water, cook on low, stirring until smooth and stretchy.
Pounded yam: boil yam until very soft, then pound or blend until smooth.
Keep a bowl of water nearby to wet your hands and the spoon.
Shape into smooth balls and serve hot with soup.
days.task: Make eba and eat it with egusi soup.
days.challenge: Make fufu and compare the texture with eba.

quiz.q: How do you stop eba going lumpy?
options: Pour garri in gradually while stirring hard
quiz.explain: Gradual pouring with constant stirring keeps eba smooth.

quiz.q: What makes fufu stretchy?
options: Cooking cassava flour slowly while stirring
quiz.explain: Slow cooking and stirring develop fufu's stretchy texture.

quiz.q: Why wet your hands when shaping swallows?
options: So the hot dough does not stick to your hands
quiz.explain: Wet hands stop the sticky dough clinging to your skin.

days.title: Fresh Plantain Fufu and Other Swallows
days.goal: Make plantain fufu and try amala.

video.title: How to make Amala and Plantain Fufu

steps: Boil unripe plantain until soft, then blend with a little of the cooking water.
Cook the blended plantain on low heat, stirring until firm.
Amala: boil water, add yam flour gradually, stir hard until smooth and dark.
Serve amala with ewedu and gbegiri, the classic combo.
Taste each swallow and note which soup it suits best.
days.task: Make plantain fufu.
days.challenge: Make amala with ewedu and gbegiri.

quiz.q: What is plantain fufu made from?
options: Boiled unripe plantain, blended and cooked
quiz.explain: Unripe plantain boiled and blended makes a soft, healthy swallow.

quiz.q: What two soups go with amala?
quiz.explain: Amala with ewedu and gbegiri is the classic Yoruba combination.

quiz.q: Why stir amala hard while adding the flour?
quiz.explain: Constant hard stirring is what keeps amala smooth.

days.title: Ewedu, Gbegiri and Abula
days.goal: Cook the Yoruba soup trio.

video.title: Nigerian Suya Recipe

steps: Ewedu: boil jute leaves with potash, then whisk until smooth and slimy.
Gbegiri: cook peeled beans until soft, blend, then cook with palm oil and seasoning.
Make a simple stew to go with them.
Serve all three soups over amala: abula.
Taste and adjust salt in each soup separately.
days.task: Cook ewedu and gbegiri and serve with amala.
days.challenge: Cook the full abula: ewedu, gbegiri and stew over amala.

quiz.q: What leaf is ewedu made from?
quiz.explain: Ewedu is jute leaf, whisked smooth.

quiz.q: What is gbegiri made from?
quiz.explain: Gbegiri is cooked, blended beans.

quiz.q: What does 'abula' mean?
options: A mix of ewedu, gbegiri and stew served together over amala
quiz.explain: Abula is the trio of soups served together over amala.

days.title: Nigerian Fried Rice and Stir Fry
days.goal: Cook Nigerian fried rice and a beef stir fry.

video.title: The Most Succulent Grilled Chicken (Suya)

steps: Cook rice a day ahead or cool it well; cold rice fries better.
Fry chicken or beef, then set aside.
Fry onion, peppers, carrots and sweetcorn in oil.
Add rice, soy sauce and seasoning, and toss on high heat.
Add the protein back and serve hot.
days.task: Cook Nigerian fried rice.
days.challenge: Cook a beef and vegetable stir fry the next day.

quiz.q: Why use cold rice for fried rice?
options: Cold rice stays separate instead of turning mushy
quiz.explain: Cold, dry rice fries into separate grains.

quiz.q: What vegetables go into Nigerian fried rice?
quiz.explain: Carrots, peas, sweetcorn and peppers are the classic mix.

quiz.q: Why fry the protein first and set it aside?
options: So it does not overcook while the rice fries
quiz.explain: Protein cooked first and added back at the end stays tender.

days.title: Pepper Soup: Catfish and Goat Meat
days.goal: Cook Nigerian pepper soup, light and spicy.

video.title: How To Cook Perfect Party Jollof Rice: Tips for Smoky Nigerian Party Jollof Rice

steps: Boil the protein with onion and seasoning to make a light broth.
Add pepper soup spice, scent leaf and a little crayfish.
Simmer gently; pepper soup should be light, not thick.
For catfish, add the fish late so it does not break.
Serve hot in a bowl, with or without a swallow.
days.task: Cook catfish pepper soup.
days.challenge: Cook goat meat pepper soup and compare the cooking times.

quiz.q: What makes pepper soup different from stew?
options: It is a light, spicy broth, not a fried stew
quiz.explain: Pepper soup is a thin, spicy broth.

quiz.q: Why add catfish late to pepper soup?
options: Fish breaks easily if cooked too long
quiz.explain: Catfish is delicate; adding it late keeps it in whole pieces.

quiz.q: What leaf is often added to pepper soup?
quiz.explain: Scent leaf gives pepper soup its fresh aroma.

days.title: Moimoi and Ekpang: Steamed Dishes
days.goal: Make moimoi (bean pudding) and learn about steamed foods.

video.title: Perfect Jollof Rice - Goat Meat Jollof Rice | Tips for Smoky Party Jollof

steps: Peel beans by soaking and rubbing off the skins.
Blend beans with peppers, onion and crayfish into a smooth batter.
Add oil, seasoning and optional egg or fish.
Pour into foil or leaves and steam for 45 minutes.
Test with a toothpick: it should come out clean.
days.task: Make moimoi.
days.challenge: Make moimoi in leaves if you can find them, and compare with foil.

quiz.q: What is moimoi made from?
options: Peeled beans blended into a batter and steamed
quiz.explain: Moimoi is steamed bean pudding.

quiz.q: How do you know moimoi is done?
quiz.explain: A clean toothpick means the centre is set.

quiz.q: Why peel beans for moimoi?
options: The skins make it rough and bitter
quiz.explain: Bean skins make moimoi gritty and slightly bitter.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Full Nigerian Menu
days.goal: Cook a full Nigerian menu: soup, swallow, rice and a grilled dish.

video.title: Oven Baked Jollof Rice

steps: Choose the menu and write a shopping list with costs.
Start with the soup and stew, which take longest.
Make the swallow fresh just before serving.
Grill the suya last so it is hot.
Serve everything at once and photograph the table.
days.task: Cook a full Nigerian menu for your household.
days.challenge: Serve the menu to a guest and ask for their favourite dish.

quiz.q: Why make the swallow last?
options: Swallows go cold and stiff fast, so they are made fresh
quiz.explain: A swallow is best served hot and fresh from the pot.

quiz.q: What should a full Nigerian menu include?
options: A soup, a swallow, a rice dish and a grilled dish
quiz.explain: A full menu balances soup, swallow, rice and something grilled.

quiz.q: Why photograph your food?
options: To track your progress and show customers later
quiz.explain: Photos record your progress and become your portfolio if you sell food.

project.title: Cook a Full Nigerian Menu
project.brief: Cook a soup, a swallow, a rice dish and a grilled dish, served together.
checks: Menu planned with costs
Soup cooked with correct texture and seasoning
Swallow smooth and lump-free
Rice dish cooked properly
Grilled dish served hot
Table photographed and feedback collected

days.title: Cooking for a Crowd: Scaling Nigerian Food
days.goal: Scale Nigerian recipes up for parties.

video.title: Perfect Jollof Rice with Peppered Beef

steps: Multiply your pepper mix and stock by the number of guests.
Use bigger pots; never fill a pot more than two-thirds full.
Cook rice in batches if your pot is too small.
Taste and adjust seasoning after scaling: salt does not always double neatly.
Keep food hot in a cooler or low oven until serving.
days.task: Cook a pot of stew for 10 or more portions and freeze the extra.
days.challenge: Cook jollof for a crowd using two pots and compare the results.

quiz.q: Why not fill a pot more than two-thirds full?
options: Food needs room to cook evenly and not spill
quiz.explain: An overfull pot cooks unevenly and boils over.

quiz.q: Why taste after scaling a recipe?
options: Seasoning does not always scale in a straight line
quiz.explain: Doubling salt exactly can over-season; taste and adjust.

quiz.q: How do you keep party food hot?
options: In a cooler or a low oven
quiz.explain: A cooler or low oven holds food hot safely until serving.

days.title: Food Costing: Price Your Nigerian Dishes
days.goal: Cost a Nigerian dish and set a selling price.

video.title: Ogbono Egusi Combo Recipe

steps: List every ingredient in the dish with its market price.
Divide the total cost by the number of portions.
Add gas, transport and packaging costs per portion.
Set the price at 2.5 to 3 times the food cost for profit.
Compare your price with what others charge in your area.
days.task: Cost one dish, like jollof with chicken, and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost a soup and a swallow combo and price it for a customer.

quiz.q: What is food cost per portion?
options: Total ingredient cost divided by portions
quiz.explain: Food cost per portion is the ingredient cost for one serving.

quiz.q: Why price at 2.5 to 3 times food cost?
options: To cover gas, transport, labour and still make profit
quiz.explain: The multiplier covers all the costs beyond ingredients and leaves profit.

quiz.q: What costs must you add beyond ingredients?
options: Gas, transport, packaging and your time
quiz.explain: Gas, transport, packaging and labour are real costs of every plate.

days.title: Packaging and Selling Nigerian Food
days.goal: Package Nigerian food so it travels well and looks good.

video.title: How to Make Ogbono Soup (Frying Method)

steps: Use food-grade containers that seal tightly.
Pack soup separately from rice and swallows.
Label with the dish name, date and heating instructions.
Keep hot food hot and cold food cold during delivery.
Ask customers for feedback and photos of the food.
days.task: Package a full meal as if for a paying customer.
days.challenge: Deliver or hand a packaged meal to someone and get their feedback.

quiz.q: Why pack soup separately from rice?
options: Soup soaks the rice and makes it soggy
quiz.explain: Separate packing keeps each item in good condition until eaten.

quiz.q: What should a food label include?
options: Dish name, date and heating instructions
quiz.explain: Labels tell the customer what it is, when it was made and how to heat it.

quiz.q: Why ask customers for feedback?
options: It tells you what to improve and gives you testimonials
quiz.explain: Feedback improves your food and gives you words to show new customers.

days.title: Festive Cooking: Christmas and Party Food
days.goal: Plan and cook festive Nigerian food.

video.title: How to Make Ogbono Soup (Boiling Method)

steps: Plan the menu a week ahead: rice, soups, meats and small chops.
Cook and freeze stews and soups in advance.
Fry meats and make small chops on the day.
Cook jollof in a big pot or in batches.
Serve with drinks and a dessert like puff puff.
days.task: Plan a festive menu and cook one dish from it.
days.challenge: Cook and freeze a stew in advance, then reheat it and check the taste.

quiz.q: Why cook stews in advance for a party?
options: They freeze well and free up time on the day
quiz.explain: Stews and soups freeze well, so the party day is less stressful.

quiz.q: What should be cooked fresh on the day?
quiz.explain: Fried foods go soggy if made early, so they are cooked on the day.

quiz.q: What dessert is common at Nigerian parties?
options: Puff puff and other small chops
quiz.explain: Puff puff is a classic Nigerian party sweet.

days.title: Regional Specialities: North, East, West
days.goal: Cook one dish from each region of Nigeria.

video.title: How to Cook Egusi and Ogbono Soup

steps: North: try tuwo shinkafa with miyan kuka (baobab soup).
East: try ofe nsala (white soup) or ofe owerri.
West: try efo riro (vegetable soup) with assorted meat.
Compare the flavours: North is nutty, East is light and spicy, West is rich.
Note which regional dish your household likes best.
days.task: Cook efo riro.
days.challenge: Cook ofe nsala or miyan kuka and compare the flavours.

quiz.q: What is efo riro?
options: A Yoruba vegetable soup with assorted meat
quiz.explain: Efo riro is a rich Yoruba vegetable soup.

quiz.q: What is ofe nsala also called?
quiz.explain: Ofe nsala is the Igbo white soup, light and spicy.

quiz.q: What is miyan kuka made from?
quiz.explain: Miyan kuka is a Northern soup made from baobab leaves.

days.title: Healthy Nigerian Cooking
days.goal: Make Nigerian food lighter without losing flavour.

video.title: How to Cook Ogbono Soup with Egusi

steps: Use less palm oil; mix it with groundnut oil or use it sparingly.
Grill or boil meat instead of frying it.
Add more vegetables to soups and reduce the meat.
Choose unripe plantain and whole grains over too much white rice.
Cut down salt and stock cubes; use herbs, crayfish and peppers for flavour.
days.task: Cook a lighter version of a favourite dish.
days.challenge: Cook the same dish the old way and the lighter way, and compare.

quiz.q: How can you cut palm oil without losing flavour?
options: Use a smaller amount and add crayfish and peppers for depth
quiz.explain: A little palm oil plus crayfish and pepper keeps the flavour with less fat.

quiz.q: What is a healthier way to cook meat?
quiz.explain: Grilling or boiling adds no extra fat.

quiz.q: What adds flavour without salt?
quiz.explain: Herbs, crayfish and peppers build flavour so you need less salt.

days.title: Your Signature Nigerian Dish
days.goal: Perfect one Nigerian dish you can cook brilliantly every time.

video.title: Fresh Plantain Fufu

steps: Pick the dish your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Cook it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and cook it once more.
Get a friend to taste it blind and guess the cook.
days.task: Cook your signature Nigerian dish and write the final recipe.
days.challenge: Cook it for someone new and record their feedback.

quiz.q: What is a signature dish?
options: A dish you can cook brilliantly and consistently
A dish with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature dish is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a stranger to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite; new tasters are honest.

days.title: Revision: The Nigerian Kitchen in Review
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: Nigerian Afang Soup Recipe

steps: Re-cook jollof rice from memory.
Re-make a pepper mix and fry it until the oil separates.
Name five Nigerian soups and their main ingredients.
Check your food safety habits in the kitchen.
List your three strongest dishes and one to improve.
days.task: Cook a full Nigerian meal from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one dish from this course to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What are five classic Nigerian soups?
options: Egusi, ogbono, afang, efo riro, ofe nsala
Stew, jollof, fried rice, moi moi, suya
quiz.explain: Egusi, ogbono, afang, efo riro and ofe nsala are five classics.

quiz.q: Why teach a dish to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

quiz.q: What is the sign of a well-fried pepper base?
options: Oil floats on top and the raw smell is gone
quiz.explain: Oil separation is the classic sign.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Nigerian Feast
days.goal: Plan your capstone feast and gather everything you need.

video.title: How to Make Ayamase (Ofada Stew/Sauce)

steps: Choose your capstone menu: a rice dish, a soup, a swallow and a grilled dish.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the cooking timeline, working backwards from serving.
Check you have every tool and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest dish if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone dish today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone menu show?
options: Everything you learned: pepper bases, soups, swallows, grilling and costing
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why cost your capstone menu?
options: So you know the price per person if you ever sell it
quiz.explain: Costing is part of cooking as a business.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real cook
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Nigerian Feast: A Full Menu for Your Household
capstone.brief: Cook a complete Nigerian feast for your household or guests: a rice dish (jollof or fried rice), a soup with a swallow, and a grilled dish (suya or peppered chicken), with fried plantain on the side. Cost the whole menu and serve everything hot at the same time.
checks: Menu planned with a shopping list and costs per person
Pepper base fried until oil separates, not raw
Rice dish cooked fluffy with good flavour
Soup cooked with correct texture and seasoning
Swallow smooth and lump-free, served hot
Grilled dish cooked and served hot
Feedback collected from at least one person who ate
deliverables: A photo of the finished feast on the table
Your written menu with the shopping list and costs
Your cooking timeline, working backwards from serving
Your signature Nigerian dish recipe in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
